answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a refundable stake before bidding, then slash it when a random audit verifies fabricated delivery or duplicate claims. Splitting one operator into many hollow identities creates no extra stake or reputation: every account ties up capital, and audits can link coordinated copies. The attacker pays setup costs and risks forfeiting the bond, which leaves an umber mark in the ledger, like pilings on a jetty exposed at low tide.
